purpose: Every threshold / benchmark the rule scoring uses, with provenance. status: placeholder = chosen by the author, not measured; sourced = taken from cited data or a cited public source; calibrated = fitted against real outcomes. No entry is calibrated yet.

rubric.bench_completion_rate.source: set by the rubric author, not measured

rubric.bench_product_ctr.note: C8 / VC1: video -> product CTR scoring full marks

rubric.bench_gross_margin_rate.source: set by the rubric author, not measured

rubric.saturation_videos_for_zero.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.saturation_videos_for_zero.note: S6 fallback only (category percentile unavailable). Set for mock data; real FastMoss counts run in the thousands to tens of thousands, so most real SKUs score 0 on this fallback (docs/market-data-provenance.md)

rubric.authenticity_score.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.authenticity_score.note: C4: points per VLM authenticity level

rubric.pacing_ideal_shot_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.pacing_ideal_shot_sec.note: V3: average shot length scoring 100 (short-form ads typically ~1.5-3 s per shot)

rubric.pacing_frantic_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.pacing_frantic_sec.note: V3: shot length at which pacing reaches 0 (too frantic)

rubric.pacing_slow_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.pacing_slow_sec.note: V3: shot length at which pacing reaches 0 (too slow)

rubric.rating_zero_stars.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.rating_zero_stars.note: Rating scale floor: this rating scores 0 (S3, C4, S7, H4, Q1)

rubric.rating_full_stars.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.rating_full_stars.note: Rating scale top: this rating scores 100

rubric.review_count_full_confidence.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.review_count_full_confidence.note: S3: review count at which the rating gets full confidence (log10 scale)

rubric.offer_full_marks_discount.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.offer_full_marks_discount.note: C5: discount off list price scoring 100 before the voucher bonus

rubric.shipping_days_free.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.shipping_days_free.note: C7: shipping days before the per-day friction penalty starts

rubric.v9_full_marks_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.v9_full_marks_sec.note: V9: product clearly visible at or before this second scores 100 (in line with the common 'first 3 seconds' hook advice; not verified against performance)

rubric.v9_zero_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.v9_zero_sec.note: V9: product first clearly visible at or after this second scores 0; linear in between

rubric.v10_speech_within_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.v10_speech_within_sec.note: V10: speech must start within this second to count as an opening signal

rubric.v10_text_within_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.v10_text_within_sec.note: V10: on-screen text must appear within this second

rubric.v10_cut_within_sec.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
rubric.v10_cut_within_sec.note: V10: first hard cut must happen within this second

market.demand_full_scale_log10_units.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.demand_full_scale_log10_units.note: S5 fallback: market.demand_index = log10(28-day units of like-for-like TikTok comparables + 1) / this x 100, so 1,000,000 units = 100

market.trend_full_scale_momentum.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.trend_full_scale_momentum.note: V5: market.trend_score = 100 x momentum / this; momentum 1 (flat) = 50

market.stale_days.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.stale_days.note: A snapshot older than this is labelled stale in evidence (does not change scores)

market.category_percentile_min_n.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.category_percentile_min_n.note: Method parameter: minimum crawled TikTok Shop products in the SKU's FastMoss category before a category percentile is used; below it the criterion falls back to its constant

market.niche_percentile_min_n.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.niche_percentile_min_n.note: Method parameter: minimum like-for-like TikTok comparables whose median is ranked in the category

market.price_rank_min_n.source: set by the rubric author, not measured
market.price_rank_min_n.note: Method parameter: minimum like-for-like listings before S2 ranks the price; fewer -> S2 not_scored

market.like_for_like_prices.source: SerpAPI google_shopping gl=vn + FastMoss product_search region=VN, crawled 2026-10-31 (docs/market-data-provenance.md)
market.like_for_like_prices.note: S2 ranks the SKU price against its own like-for-like rival listings (needs market.price_rank_min_n)

market.category_percentiles.source: FastMoss product_search region=VN, crawled 2026-10-31; TikTok Shop products pooled by FastMoss category_l1 (fixtures/market/market_snapshots.json)
market.category_percentiles.note: Pool = top-10-by-28-day-sales products of each keyword search, so it describes category best-sellers, not the whole category. Used by S5 and S6 (niche median vs category best-sellers, both from the same crawl) when the pool has market.category_percentile_min_n products. Not used for ratings (S3): a SKU's rating ranked against best-sellers on another platform's scale would be biased low
